children: CryptoUK has called on the UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) to clarify that developing and governing decentralized finance (DeFi) protocols should not, by itself, be treated as a regulated activity. According to Odaily, in its response to the FCA’s consultation paper CP26/36, the association said software development, maintenance, security work and participation in decentralized governance should not constitute regulated activities, consistent with the FCA’s approach of identifying “clear controllers” in DeFi.

CryptoUK broadly supports the FCA’s draft guidance but said some provisions exceed the scope of legislation, including using the location of protocol development and governance as a basis for establishing a UK connection and imposing requirements on payment and own-account trading exemptions. The association also urged the FCA to publish a public list of stablecoins that comply with the UK regulatory framework and clarify the distinction between stablecoins and electronic money.

title: CryptoUK Urges FCA to Clarify DeFi Development Is Not Automatically a Regulated Activity
